subject: Interruption: targeted cloud peering in us-east + eu-west — immediate mitigation steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Murphy <ryan.murphy@big-retail.com>, ops@acme-cloud.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interruption: targeted cloud peering in us-east + eu-west — immediate mitigation steps

Hi Ryan / Acme Ops team,

We’re alerting you to a degraded availability window affecting requests routed through two provider peering points (US-East and EU-West). Impact: elevated latencies and a small number of failed requests for tenants with strict region affinity. Our monitoring shows the provider experienced a BGP flap that caused transient route blackholing for some paths.

What we are doing now:
- Triggered automatic fallback to alternate regions where possible and increased request retries for compatible model variants.
- Enabled temporary broadened routing for affected tenants to keep requests flowing (no model switch for private-only deployments unless explicitly allowed).

Recommended immediate customer actions (low friction):
1) If you can tolerate cross-region routing for the next 2–6 hours, set region_preference to "best_available" for your API key or tenant to accept fallback endpoints. Example: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/prefs { "region_preference": "best_available" }
2) If you require strict in-region execution, reduce parallel concurrency to avoid request queueing and set client timeout to 8s to surface failures faster.
3) If you want us to apply a tenant-level override, reply with your tenant id and a single-sentence opt-in (we’ll apply and audit it).

We’ve attached a quick outage map and a CSV template for tenant overrides.

Status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2029-03-20-peering-flap

Sorry for the disruption — we’ll keep updates coming.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Fwd: Re: Interruption: targeted cloud peering — runbook + tenant override

Laura / Ben — attaching the minimal runbook and commands. We validated this in staging and it preserves KV cache consistency when switching affinity. High level:

What the override does:
- Sets tenant.routing.allow_fallback = true
- Adds an audit event with operator id and TTL
- Optionally pins to a sidecar proxy in an alternate region if tenant requires data locality but can accept a proxy hop

CLI / API snippets (example):
1) Self-serve (customer):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/T-12345/prefs -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \n  -d '{"routing": {"allow_fallback": true, "fallback_ttl_seconds": 28800}}'

2) Apply on behalf (internal):
redwood tenant update T-12345 --set routing.allow_fallback=true --set routing.fallback_ttl_seconds=28800 --operator laura.bennett

Operational checks:
- Verify KV cache flush for tenant: redwood cache flush T-12345 --confirm
- Verify endpoint preference: redwood tenant get T-12345 | grep allow_fallback
- TTL auto-reversion observed in 8 hours in tenant audit log (audit id in response)

We will attach runbook-commands.txt to RED-7892 and have SRE on standby for manual rollback.

— Markus

Subject: Post-incident update: targeted peering flap (US-East, EU-West) — actions taken and next steps

Hi Ryan / Acme Ops / team,

Follow-up to the outage earlier this week. Summary and RCA at a glance:
- What happened: Provider BGP instability at two peering points (US-East and EU-West) caused transient blackholing for a subset of routes used by our edge proxies.
- What we did: Automatically routed traffic to alternate edges when possible, offered tenant-level overrides, and coordinated with the provider for expedited remediation.
- Customer impact: ~12 minutes median elevated latency window for affected tenants, <0.03% increased error rate overall. Tenants with strict region affinity that kept in-region enforcement saw failed requests unless they opted in to fallback.

Tenant-specific outcomes for Big Retail:
- You chose conservative posture; we did not apply any override without explicit opt-in.
- We can apply a timeboxed override for your tenant if you confirm, and we’ll include an audit entry and immediate visibility in the tenant activity feed.

Compensation / credits:
We are proposing a one-time service credit for impacted API units for the window between 09:04–09:16 PST. I’ll coordinate with Billing once you confirm an opt-in/override decision.

Next steps and where to find more details:
- Full postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/2029-03-20-peering-bridge-postmortem
- Ticket: JIRA RED-7892 (runbook, audit IDs attached)
- If you want the override now, reply with: "Apply override: T-12345, TTL 8h"

Thanks again for the patience — root cause and provider mitigations are documented in the postmortem draft.

— Laura

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2029 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Peering flap postmortem and confirmation request

Hi Ryan — quick final note to close the loop. The postmortem has been finalized and made public to your incident contacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/2029-03-20-peering-bridge-postmortem

Highlights:
- Root cause: intermittent BGP route withdrawal at provider edge (software bug on provider router).
- Fix: provider deployed control-plane patch; they’ve committed enhanced BGP convergence testing for the region.
- Our takeaways: improve tenant-level opt-in tooling, add an automated audit entry for all manual overrides, and reduce default DNS TTL to 30s for edge endpoints during elevated risk windows.

Attached: outage-map.png, runbook-commands.txt. Please confirm whether you want the temporary override applied (reply with "Apply override: T-12345, TTL 8h") or if you prefer no change.

Appreciate any feedback on the communication cadence and the runbook artifacts.

— Laura
